tests.title: Common.Register adds an --output flag defaulting to empty
tests.when: Common.Register(fs) is called and fs.Parse is run with no --output argument
then: fs.Lookup("output") is non-nil
Common.Output equals the empty string
tests.pseudocode: fs := flag.NewFlagSet(...); c := &Common{}; c.Register(fs); fs.Parse([]); assert fs.Lookup("output") != nil; assert c.Output == ""

tests.title: --output resolves against the process working directory, not --dir
given: cwd is a known temp directory
--dir points at a different, unrelated workspace directory
tests.when: --output is given a relative path alongside an unrelated --dir
then: the resolved destination equals filepath.Abs(cwd, the given value)
the resolved destination does not fall under --dir's root
tests.pseudocode: cwd, _ := os.Getwd(); resolved := resolveOutput("sub/out.json"); assert resolved == filepath.Join(cwd, "sub/out.json"); assert !strings.HasPrefix(resolved, dirFlagAbs)

tests.title: --output - is refused as a usage error before anything is fetched
tests.when: the tool is invoked with --output - and a valid positional input
then: the process exit code is 2
env.Error.Category == "usage"
no file is read or written for --output
Exec is never called
tests.pseudocode: env, code, _ := runApp(app, []string{"--output", "-", "some report"}, ""); assert code == ExitUsage; assert env.Error.Category == "usage"; assert !execCalled

tests.title: An --output path that already exists as a directory is a usage error caught before anything is fetched
given: a temp directory D exists on disk
tests.when: the tool is invoked with --output D and a valid positional input
then: the process exit code is 2
env.Error.Category == "usage"
Exec is never called
tests.pseudocode: env, code, _ := runApp(app, []string{"--output", tempDir, "some report"}, ""); assert code == ExitUsage; assert !execCalled

tests.title: --output validation runs once, before PreCheck, Workspace(), Resolve or model resolution
given: an App whose PreCheck, CheckInput and Exec each set a flag when called
tests.when: the tool is invoked with --output - (a malformed value) and a valid positional input
then: the run fails with exit code 2 before PreCheck ran
Workspace() was never called
no model was resolved
Exec was never called
tests.pseudocode: app.PreCheck = func(*Common) error { preCheckCalled = true; return nil }; code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--output", "-", "x"}, ...); assert code == ExitUsage; assert !preCheckCalled; assert !execCalled

tests.title: The end-of-Main envelope is fully written to --output before any byte reaches stdout
given: an App whose Exec returns a deterministic successful result
--output points at a fresh path in a temp directory
tests.when: app.Main runs to completion with a stdout writer that, on its first Write, reads and parses the --output file
then: at the moment stdout receives its first byte, the file at --output already exists and unmarshals into a complete envelope
that envelope's Tool, ExitCode and Result match the envelope subsequently written to stdout
tests.pseudocode: type probeWriter struct{ outPath string }; func (p *probeWriter) Write(b []byte) (int, error) { data, err := os.ReadFile(p.outPath); assert err == nil; var e Envelope; assert json.Unmarshal(data, &e) == nil; return len(b), nil }; code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--output", outPath, "x"}, stdin, &probeWriter{outPath}, stderr)

tests.title: The flag-parsing-failure envelope is written to --output before stdout, when --output parsed before the bad flag
given: --output is given before an undefined flag on the command line
tests.when: app.Main is invoked with argv = ["--output", outPath, "--nope", "x"]
then: the process exit code is 2
the file at --output exists and unmarshals to the same usage-failure envelope written to stdout
tests.pseudocode: code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--output", outPath, "--nope", "x"}, stdin, &stdout, &stderr); assert code == ExitUsage; fileEnv := readEnvelope(outPath); stdoutEnv := readEnvelope(stdout.Bytes()); assert fileEnv == stdoutEnv

tests.title: Emit's marshal-failure fallback envelope is written to --output identically to stdout
given: an envelope whose Result field cannot be marshalled to JSON (e.g. a channel)
Output is set on the Run/Emit call
tests.when: EmitWithOutput(w, outPath, env) is called
then: the return code is ExitFailed
the file at outPath exists and its content, byte for byte, equals what was written to w
tests.pseudocode: env := r.Envelope(ExitOK, map[string]any{"bad": make(chan int)}, nil); code := EmitWithOutput(&buf, outPath, env); assert code == ExitFailed; fileBytes, _ := os.ReadFile(outPath); assert bytes.Equal(fileBytes, buf.Bytes())

tests.title: The --output file always carries exactly the same envelope stdout receives, outside a report-file collision
given: no --report-file collision configured
tests.when: for any combination of exit code (OK, failed, usage, needs_human, unverified), result payload, and set of warnings, the run is made with --output set
then: the parsed content of the --output file deep-equals the parsed content written to stdout for that same run
tests.pseudocode: for (code, result, warnings) in gen_envelopes(): env := buildEnvelope(code, result, warnings); stdoutEnv, fileEnv := runWithOutput(env); assert deepEqual(stdoutEnv, fileEnv)

tests.title: A write to --output is always atomic: no partial content is ever observable and no temp file survives
tests.when: for any envelope whose serialised size ranges from a few bytes to several megabytes, it is written to --output
then: a goroutine polling the destination path throughout the write never reads a document that fails to parse as complete JSON
after the write returns, the target directory contains no leftover temp file
the file at the destination equals the envelope written
tests.pseudocode: for size in gen_sizes(): env := buildEnvelopeOfSize(size); done := make(chan struct{}); go pollDuringWrite(outPath, done); writeAtomic(outPath, env); close(done); assert noPartialReadObserved; assert !hasTempFilesIn(dir(outPath))

tests.title: A missing parent directory for --output is created at write time
given: --output points inside a directory tree that does not yet exist
tests.when: the run completes and the envelope is written to --output
then: the parent directory now exists
the file at --output exists and contains the envelope
tests.pseudocode: outPath := filepath.Join(tempDir, "a", "b", "c", "out.json"); code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--output", outPath, "x"}, ...); _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Dir(outPath)); assert err == nil; _, err = os.Stat(outPath); assert err == nil

tests.title: --output is written under --dry-run exactly as without it
given: a tool that accepts --dry-run and behaves identically apart from remote effects
tests.when: the same run is made once with --dry-run and once without it, both with --output set to distinct paths
then: both --output files exist and contain a complete envelope
the two envelopes' Tool, Result and Warnings fields match apart from any dry-run-specific field
tests.pseudocode: runApp(app, []string{"--dry-run", "--output", outA, "x"}, ""); runApp(app, []string{"--output", outB, "x"}, ""); assert fileExists(outA); assert fileExists(outB)

tests.title: -h/--help performs no --output validation and writes no file, even for a malformed --output value
given: --output is set to "-", which would otherwise be a usage error
tests.when: the tool is invoked with -h --output -
then: the exit code is 0
stdout is empty
no file named "-" is created
no usage error about --output is reported
tests.pseudocode: var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer; code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"-h", "--output", "-"}, stdin, &stdout, &stderr); assert code == ExitOK; assert stdout.Len() == 0; assert !fileExists("-")

tests.title: A bare invocation with no positional argument performs no --output validation and writes no file
given: --output is set to an existing directory, which would otherwise be a usage error
tests.when: the tool is invoked with only --output <existing-dir> and no positional argument
then: stdout is empty
no envelope is emitted
no file or error about the existing-directory --output value is produced
tests.pseudocode: var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer; code := app.Main(ctx, []string{"--output", existingDir}, stdin, &stdout, &stderr); assert stdout.Len() == 0; assert code == ExitUsage; assert !strings.Contains(stderr.String(), "output")

tests.title: --output never changes ok, status or exit_code
tests.when: for any exit code among {OK, failed, usage, needs_human, unverified}, crossed with --output unset, --output set and succeeding, and --output set but failing to write
then: OK and ExitCode on the run's own envelope are identical across all three --output states for the same underlying exit code
tests.pseudocode: for code in exitCodes: baseline := runWithoutOutput(code); withOutput := runWithOutput(code, outPath); withFailingOutput := runWithOutput(code, unwritablePath); assert baseline.OK == withOutput.OK == withFailingOutput.OK; assert baseline.ExitCode == withOutput.ExitCode == withFailingOutput.ExitCode

tests.title: A failed --output write is a low-severity output_not_written warning visible on the same run's stdout envelope, with the exit code unaffected
given: --output points at a path under a directory the process cannot create (permission denied)
tests.when: a successful run completes with that --output value
then: the process exit code and ok match what they would be without --output
env.Warnings contains an entry with code output_not_written, severity low, stage emit, naming the path and the underlying error
that warning is present on the stdout envelope produced for this same invocation
tests.pseudocode: env, code, _ := runApp(app, []string{"--output", unwritablePath, "x"}, ""); assert code == ExitOK; assert env.OK; w := findWarning(env.Warnings, "output_not_written"); assert w != nil; assert w.Severity == "low"; assert w.Stage == "emit"; assert strings.Contains(w.Message, unwritablePath)

tests.title: The central WarnCode table maps output_not_written to stage emit
tests.when: the WarnCode-to-stage table is queried for output_not_written
then: the table contains output_not_written
its recorded stage is emit
tests.pseudocode: stage, ok := WarnStages["output_not_written"]; assert ok; assert stage == "emit"

tests.title: When Emit's own fallback envelope also fails to write to --output, no second warnings entry is added
given: a result that cannot be marshalled to JSON
--output points at a destination that itself cannot be written
tests.when: EmitWithOutput is called with that envelope and that --output path
then: the stdout content is the minimal fallback envelope carrying only the marshal failure
that fallback envelope's warnings field carries no output_not_written entry
the underlying write error is not surfaced as a second, separate warning anywhere
tests.pseudocode: env := r.Envelope(ExitOK, map[string]any{"bad": make(chan int)}, nil); code := EmitWithOutput(&buf, unwritablePath, env); var got Envelope; json.Unmarshal(buf.Bytes(), &got); assert findWarning(got.Warnings, "output_not_written") == nil

tests.title: --output and --report-file are compared as resolved, absolute, cleaned paths, without resolving symlinks
given: two literal path strings that clean to the same absolute path (e.g. "a/../a/out.json" and "a/out.json") but where neither file exists yet
tests.when: the collision check runs over these two configured values
then: the two are reported as colliding, because filepath.Abs+filepath.Clean of each is equal
no attempt is made to resolve either as a symlink before comparing
tests.pseudocode: a := "a/../a/out.json"; b := "a/out.json"; assert configuredDestinationsCollide(a, b) == true

tests.title: Collision detection depends only on the two configured, cleaned paths, never on whether either write succeeds
tests.when: for any pair of path strings, and for any combination of --output-write-succeeds and --report-file-write-succeeds outcomes
then: the collision verdict for that pair is identical across all four success/failure combinations, and equals whether filepath.Clean(filepath.Abs(a)) == filepath.Clean(filepath.Abs(b))
tests.pseudocode: for (a, b) in gen_path_pairs(): want := clean(abs(a)) == clean(abs(b)); for (outOK, reportOK) in [(true,true),(true,false),(false,true),(false,false)]: got := runCollisionCheck(a, b, outOK, reportOK); assert got == want

tests.title: On a configured collision, --output's own write is skipped and the complete report lands, with a warning naming the collision
given: --output and --report-file are given the same literal path
the report-file write itself succeeds and writes the complete, full-detail report
tests.when: the tool runs to completion with --detail summary --output P --report-file P
then: no attempted --output write, successful or failed, occurs at P (no output_not_written warning appears)
the file at P holds the complete report, not the --detail-selected view
env.Warnings contains output_matches_report_file, severity low, stage emit
tests.pseudocode: env, code, _ := runApp(app, []string{"--detail", "summary", "--output", p, "--report-file", p, "x"}, ""); assert code == ExitOK; content := readFile(p); assert isFullReport(content); assert findWarning(env.Warnings, "output_matches_report_file") != nil; assert findWarning(env.Warnings, "output_not_written") == nil

tests.title: When the collided destination's report-file write itself fails, nothing lands there and both causes are named
given: --output and --report-file resolve to the same path P
P's write fails (e.g. P's parent cannot be created)
tests.when: the tool runs to completion with --output P --report-file P
then: no file exists at P after the run
env.Warnings contains both output_matches_report_file and report_file_not_written
the run's exit code and ok are unaffected by either failure
tests.pseudocode: env, code, _ := runApp(app, []string{"--output", p, "--report-file", p, "x"}, ""); assert !fileExists(p); assert findWarning(env.Warnings, "output_matches_report_file") != nil; assert findWarning(env.Warnings, "report_file_not_written") != nil; assert code == ExitOK

tests.title: The central WarnCode table maps output_matches_report_file to stage emit
tests.when: the WarnCode-to-stage table is queried for output_matches_report_file
then: the table contains output_matches_report_file
its recorded stage is emit
tests.pseudocode: stage, ok := WarnStages["output_matches_report_file"]; assert ok; assert stage == "emit"

tests.title: docs/cli.md's shared-flags table documents --output, its atomicity, its ordering before stdout, and the report-file collision
tests.when: docs/cli.md is read
then: the shared-flags table contains a row for --output
that row's description mentions writing a second copy of the envelope stdout gets
it mentions the write is atomic and happens before stdout
it describes what happens when --output collides with --report-file
tests.pseudocode: text := readFile("docs/cli.md"); assert strings.Contains(text, "--output"); assert strings.Contains(text, "atomic"); assert strings.Contains(text, "before"); assert strings.Contains(text, "--report-file")

tests.title: docs/cli.md's warning-codes table lists output_not_written and output_matches_report_file
tests.when: docs/cli.md is read
then: the warning-codes table contains a row for output_not_written
the warning-codes table contains a row for output_matches_report_file
both rows appear alongside report_file_not_written
tests.pseudocode: text := readFile("docs/cli.md"); assert strings.Contains(text, "output_not_written"); assert strings.Contains(text, "output_matches_report_file"); assert strings.Contains(text, "report_file_not_written")

tests.title: A supervisor that has already lost its own stdout still recovers the full result from --output
given: fix is invoked against a real git repository with a real GitHub-shaped forge server
the supervisor's stdout pipe is closed the instant the process exits
tests.when: fix runs to completion with --output pointed at a durable path, landing a pull request
then: the file at --output exists and, read after the process exits, unmarshals to one complete JSON envelope
that envelope's ok, result and pull-request URL match what a caller with an intact stdout would have seen
no partially-written document is ever observed at the path

tests.title: A failed --output write is downgraded to a warning and never changes impl's exit code
given: impl is invoked against a real git repository and a real forge server
--output names a destination under a directory the process cannot create
tests.when: impl runs a full implementation task to completion with that --output value
then: the run exits 0 and ok is true, exactly as it would without --output
the stdout envelope carries a low-severity output_not_written warning naming the path and the underlying cause
no file is left at the unwritable --output path

tests.title: spec's --output and --report-file, pointed at the same path, land the complete report rather than the --detail view
given: spec is invoked against a real repository
--detail summary --output ./run.json --report-file ./run.json are all given
tests.when: spec runs to completion generating a full specification package
then: the file at ./run.json holds the complete report, not the --detail summary view
the stdout envelope carries the output_matches_report_file warning
no separate write attempt happened for --output at that path

tests.title: Emit's internal marshal-failure fallback still leaves a durable, minimal envelope at --output
given: fix's Exec returns a result value carrying a field that cannot be marshalled to JSON
--output points at a fresh, writable path
tests.when: app.Main runs to completion with that Exec and that --output value
then: stdout carries the minimal fallback envelope naming the marshal failure
the file at --output exists and, parsed, is byte-for-byte identical to that same fallback envelope
no full result envelope is ever observed at either destination
